name: Visualization Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building visualization — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary visualization tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building visualization — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary visualization tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Check that visualization terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
2. Keep visualization changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. When visualization decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
4. Prefer explicit, readable visualization solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. Before starting visualization work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
6. Keep visualization outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen visualization approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting visualization assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not apply generic visualization advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated visualization concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new visualization abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop visualization edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for visualization, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
